content: Confirmed decision: Suppress injection during compaction retries. Keep the snapshot available for a later normal request.
provenance: reconstructed evaluation conversation, not a verbatim session transcript

source_evidence.excerpt: - Keep `experimental.chat.messages.transform` as a no-op. Because OpenCode 1.18.18 also reaches `experimental.chat.system.transform` for compaction, synchronously track the latest newly created native assistant request per session from `message.updated`; suppress injection while that marker is the compaction summary, across all provider retries, without consuming the active snapshot.

Native context injection uses each runner's supported model-visible field. Codex memory injection with Supermemory selected is performed by the official plugin's hooks. OpenCode injection uses `experimental.chat.system.transform` to add bounded advisory text to the model-visible system context for each normal request in the active logical user turn. OpenCode keeps `experimental.chat.messages.transform` as a no-op. Because OpenCode compaction also reaches `experimental.chat.system.transform`, Deck suppresses system injection while the latest native assistant request marker is the compaction summary; compaction retries do not consume or delete the active turn snapshot, and a later normal request marker or trusted user turn restores injection. Pi's `deck-memory` extension appends bounded advisory text to the system prompt of the current turn only (an ephemeral `before_agent_start` return, never a persisted message, so it cannot accumulate across turns or sessions). Runner hooks receive only Deck's ephemeral loopback endpoint/token; they never receive `containerTag` or provider credentials.

A reproduced prompt produced Adaptive Context = YES for inference 1, invoked the mandatory `deck-lead` skill, then produced Adaptive Context = NO for inference 2. A second user message in the same native session did not reevaluate retrieval policy. The implementation therefore had `recall once per session + inject once per inference` semantics instead of `recall once per eligible logical user turn + inject for every inference in that turn`.

source_evidence.excerpt: `apps/cli/src/tui/app.tsx:776-791` resolves the catalog lookup key from `packages[i].name`, but the value passed in is `action.source` (`"oraios/serena"`) rather than the catalog id (`"serena"`). The catalog filter therefore matches zero rows and the callback short-circuits to "already installed" with `success: true`. The `action-runner` then synthesizes a misleading `Installed oraios/serena.` message because none of the per-package results failed.

content: Confirmed convention: persist project preferences in .harbor/settings.json. There is no global user-preferences store. Confirmed convention: use Changesets markdown for change plans and ADR markdown for design decisions. Do not create OpenSpec state.yaml or events.yaml. Confirmed convention: plugin hosts own plugin-specific routing policy. The shared @harbor/kernel contains only data types and has no canonical capability selection policy. Confirmed convention: tests live beside source as *.spec.ts and run with bun test. Confirmed convention: release versions for packages are independent; there is no repository-wide lockstep version.
Confirmed convention: Deck user preferences use the global XDG configuration; OpenSpec is authoritative for changes; @deck/core owns provider-neutral policy.

source_evidence.excerpt: `@deck/core` owns runner-neutral concepts: configuration, capability contracts, developer-team content, skills, and registry primitives. `@deck/sdd-runtime` owns SDD contracts, orchestration, runner coordination, and artifact-state operations. It is a runtime boundary rather than a documentation inventory.

Make `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deck/config.json` (default `~/.config/deck/config.json`) the only active source for Deck user and runner preferences. Project roots remain execution/materialization targets, never preference roots. Existing local and legacy configs are preserved as migration inputs and are never silently overwritten or deleted.
